title: Upgrade readiness
subtitle: Check whether a cluster is ready for a Kubernetes upgrade: deprecated and removed APIs, component compatibility, and what the check could not see
hint: Read-only: Kubron reads cluster objects and changes nothing. Without a target version only already deprecated APIs are reported.
empty: Select a cluster and run a check, or open a report from the history.
disclaimer: This is an assessment, not a guarantee that the upgrade will succeed. Generic Kubernetes mode: provider-specific checks are not performed.

none.blocker: No blockers were found in what was checked.
none.warning: No warnings were found in what was checked.

coverage.title: Coverage: what was and was not checked
coverage.lead: Read this first: the report covers only the sources listed as checked. Anything else was not examined, and no conclusion about it is made.

diff.title: What changed since the previous check
diff.first: This is the first check of this cluster: there is nothing to compare with.
diff.targetChanged: The target version differs ({before} → {after}): the findings answer a different question.

actions.note: These are recommendations. Kubron does not change the cluster and does not run the upgrade.

history.title: History
history.empty: No checks yet for this cluster.

export.copyFailed: Could not copy to the clipboard

action.backup: Make sure you can restore the cluster: take a backup using the procedure of your distribution or provider.
action.checkManifests: Check the manifests in Git or GitOps repositories for deprecated and removed APIs: Kubron analyzes only live cluster objects.
action.fixUnhealthy: Fix the components that are not ready.
action.migrateDeprecatedAPIs: Plan the migration of objects that use deprecated APIs.
action.migrateRemovedAPIs: Migrate all objects that use APIs removed in the target version, and update the manifests that produce them.
action.planStepwise: Split the upgrade into single minor version steps.
action.readReleaseNotes: Read the release notes of the target Kubernetes version.
action.rerunReadiness: After the upgrade, run the readiness check again and compare it with this report.
action.resolveComponents: Resolve the documented component limitations before upgrading.
action.reviewNotChecked: Review the areas marked "not checked"; the report does not cover them.
action.reviewUnrecognized: Review the components that are not in the catalog; Kubron did not check their compatibility.
action.verifyAddons: After the upgrade, check the add-ons (CNI, DNS, ingress, metrics) against their documentation.
action.verifyComponentDocs: Confirm compatibility of the components marked "not enough data" in their projects' documentation.
action.verifyNodesReady: After the upgrade, check that all nodes are Ready and run the target version.
action.verifyWorkloads: After the upgrade, check that system workloads and your applications are healthy.

api.deprecated: {kind} ({apiVersion}) is deprecated since Kubernetes {deprecatedIn}; {count} object(s) in the cluster were created or managed with this API version.
api.migrate: Migrate these manifests to {replacement} before upgrading.
api.migrateNoReplacement: Migrate to a supported API version; the upstream data names no direct replacement. See the deprecation guide.
api.removed: {kind} ({apiVersion}) is removed in Kubernetes {target} (removed in {removedIn}); {count} object(s) in the cluster were created or managed with this API version.

catalog.noMatchingRule: The catalog has no rule that covers this component version with the target Kubernetes version.
catalog.noRules: The catalog has no compatibility rules for this component: its project documentation does not allow deriving them.

component.confirmed: {name} {version} is documented by the project as compatible with Kubernetes {target}.
component.insufficientData: The compatibility of {name} {version} with Kubernetes {target} could not be confirmed from the catalog: not enough data. This is not a confirmation of compatibility.
component.knownLimitation: The project documents a limitation for {name} {version} with Kubernetes {target}.
component.notReady: {name} is not fully ready ({ready} of {desired} instances).
component.notRecognized: {name} is not in the component catalog; its compatibility with Kubernetes {target} was not checked.

live.componentsCatalogOnly: Components are matched against a limited catalog by workload name and image; anything else is reported as not recognized.
live.customResources: Custom resources are not scanned for API usage.
live.helmReleases: Helm releases and chart templates are not analyzed.
live.kindsScanned: Only API kinds that Kubron is allowed to read were scanned (see the list of scanned and not covered kinds).
live.managedFieldsOnly: API usage is detected from managedFields and the last-applied-configuration annotation of live objects; objects without them are not covered.
live.onlyLiveObjects: Only live cluster objects are analyzed.
live.readClientsInvisible: Clients that only read an API (controllers, scripts) leave no trace in objects and are not detected.

matrix.clusterOlderThanData: The cluster version is older than the oldest release the API matrix covers; APIs removed earlier are not listed.
matrix.staleForCluster: The cluster runs a Kubernetes version newer than the API matrix knows; the matrix is out of date for this cluster.

coverage.noTarget: No target version was chosen: APIs are evaluated against the current version, so only already deprecated APIs are reported.
coverage.notAGuarantee: The report is an assessment, not a guarantee that the upgrade will succeed.

provider.notChecked: Generic Kubernetes mode: provider-specific checks (EKS, GKE, AKS and others) are not performed, and the report is not a full check of a managed service.

source.notAnalyzed: This source is not analyzed in this version, so nothing was checked in it.

ingress-nginx.retired: Ingress NGINX is retired by the Kubernetes project: no further releases or security fixes.

metrics-server.beyond-matrix: The project lists this Metrics Server series as supported only up to Kubernetes 1.21.

platform.currentUnsupported: Kubernetes {current} is older than the versions upstream currently supports ({window}).

path.ok: The upgrade from {current} to {target} is a single minor version step.
path.sameVersion: The target version equals the current version; only patch-level changes are possible.
path.skipsMinor: The upgrade from {current} to {target} spans {steps} minor versions; Kubernetes supports upgrading the control plane one minor version at a time.

component.limitation: Review the documented limitation and upgrade or replace the component before upgrading Kubernetes.
component.unhealthy: Bring the component to a healthy state before upgrading.
component.unrecognized: Check manually whether this component supports the target Kubernetes version.
component.verify: Check the project's compatibility documentation for this component and version against the target Kubernetes version.

platform.stepwise: Upgrade the control plane one minor version at a time.
platform.supportedVersion: Plan the move to a Kubernetes version that upstream still supports.

source.rerun: Repeat the check when the source is available, or check this area manually.

skew.newerThanAPIServer: The version is newer than the target kube-apiserver, which the version skew policy does not allow.
skew.targetUnknown: The version could not be compared with the target version.
skew.tooOld: The version is older than the Kubernetes version skew policy allows for the target version.
skew.within: The version is within the Kubernetes version skew policy for the target version.

api.notCovered: {count} API kind(s) with deprecated or removed versions cannot be read by Kubron; usage of them was not checked: {kinds}.

list.truncated: The list of {kinds} was larger than the read limit; only the first objects were checked.
list.unavailable: Objects of {kinds} could not be read; their API usage was not checked.

nodes.unavailable: Nodes could not be read; kubelet versions were not checked.

resources.partial: The list of served APIs was read only partially (unavailable: {failed}).
resources.unavailable: The list of served APIs could not be read; deprecated and removed API usage was not checked.

workloads.truncated: The list of workloads in {namespaces} was larger than the read limit; some components may be missing from the report.
workloads.unavailable: Workloads in {namespaces} could not be read; the components there were not checked.

version.unknown: The component version could not be determined from the image tag.
